topics.title: Exterior angles
topics.text:
If a regular polygon has exterior angles of 7.5 degrees, how many sides does it have?



SolutionThis means the polygon has interior angles of 172.5 degrees. If s is the number of sides:

$$(180s-360)/s = 172.5$$$$180s-360 = 172.5s$$$$7.5s=360$$$$s=48$$

topics.title: The slippery numbers... :)
topics.text:
The number 20 is a "slippery" number, because 20 = 10 + 10 and

1/10+1/10= 0.20, which is written as the number 20, simply preceded by zero and a comma.

A slippery number is a number that you can break into a sum of two integers a and b, not necessarily equal, let the sum of the inversions of a and b be written (according to 0)

with the digits o starting number, written in the same order they precede a zero and a comma.

How many other slippery numbers are there?

topics.title: Counting Question
topics.text:
Given that 8 students sit in a circle, how many seating arrangements are there if two arrangements are the same when at least 1 student has the same left-student and right-student as another arrangement?



So for instance, if the pre-circle arrangement was $ABCDEFGH$(in a circle of course), then a valid arrangement would be $ABECDGFH$, since $A$ is the only one that has the same left and right neighbor($B$ and $H$ respectively). Notice that in this problem, left or right is determined from each letter's perspective.

There is a special vending machine in a school, and the way this vending machine works is that it has 7 potatoes, and 1 lollipop. Kid #2 gets a potato (6/7 chance)

Kid #3 gets a potato (5/6 chance)

Kid #4 gets a lollipop (1/5 chance)

Kid #5 gets a potato (4/4 chance)

Kid #6 gets a potato (3/3 chance)

Kid #7 gets a potato (2/2 chance)

Kid #8 gets a potato (1/1 chance)

topics.title: Draw marbles
topics.text:
A big box contains marbles of one or more colors. You're given the number of marbles of each color. You draw n marbles randomly from the box, leaving each marble outside the box after taking it. Find the probability that all marbles drawn will be the same color.

Ex :

There are 3 colors. You draw 2 marbles. There 5 five marbles from first color, 6 from second colro, 7 from third color.

topics.title: Infinite Sum?
topics.text:
I was wondering if there was a way to solve this infinite sum:

$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^2}$

I know you can evaluate infinite series withe the formula, $a_1/(1 - r)$, where $r$ is the constant ratio. However, $n^2$ isn't linear.



EDIT: I read the solution is $pi^2/6$, but why?

topics.title: 2008 Chapter Sprint #22
topics.text:
Hello,



How would you solve this problem: A fair, twenty-faced die has $19$ of its faces numbered from $1$ through $19$ and has one blank face. Another fair, twenty-faced die has $19$ of its faces numbered from $1$ through $8$ and $10$ through $20$ and has one blank face. When the two dice are rolled, what is the probability that the sum of the two numbers facing up will be $24$? Express your answer as a common fraction.



Thanks,



nbute



BTW: I wasn't able to find this problem using the search feature which is why I made this thread.
